# Housing demand {#sec-demand}

<!-- Purpose: who lives in the region and how demand is changing — population, components

     + bullet findings + callouts only — no drafted prose. Built in Task 7. -->



::: {.callout-note}
## Since 2022

The 2022 Data Update projected the primary region would reach
**1,338,306 residents by 2050**, growth of
**+29%** from 2020. The Weldon Cooper Center's updated 2025-release
projections now put the 2050 total at **1,351,819**
(**30.5%** growth), a
1.0% upward revision
of the 2050 figure. The region's growth outlook has strengthened, not softened, since
the Framework was published.
:::

## The region's population continues to grow


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Over 50,000 new residents since the 2020 census](demand_files/figure-html/fig-pop-trend-1.png){#fig-pop-trend fig-align='left' fig-alt='Line chart of total population in the four primary Richmond region localities. Annual population estimates from 2020 to 2025 are highlighted in green, showing continued growth. Decennial census counts for 2000, 2010, and 2020 are shown muted in the background for long-term context.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **The core region added about 58,000 residents between the 2020 census and the 2025 population estimate, growth of 5.6% in five years.**
- Every year from 2020 to 2025 added population, with the largest single-year gains in 2024 and 2025.

## Most growth still comes from people moving into region


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Migration, not births, drives the region's population growth](demand_files/figure-html/fig-components-1.png){#fig-components fig-align='left' fig-alt='Grouped bar chart of annual components of population change in the four primary localities, 2021 to 2025. Net migration bars are substantially larger than natural change bars in every year. Natural change (births minus deaths) stays small — well under 2,000 residents per year.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **Net migration has delivered the large majority of the region's growth every year since 2021, peaking at roughly 13,300 net movers in 2024.**
- Natural change (births minus deaths) has stayed small — under about 2,100 residents per year regionwide — reflecting an aging population.
- Overall, the region's demand pressure is *primarily* driven by households arriving from elsewhere, who need housing upon arrival.
- The 2020 estimate period covers only April-June 2020 and is omitted from the chart.

## Every locality is projected to keep growing


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Chesterfield is projected to pass 500,000 residents by 2050](demand_files/figure-html/fig-projections-1.png){#fig-projections fig-align='left' fig-alt='Line chart of projected total population for the four primary localities from the 2020 census to 2050. Chesterfield rises from about 365,000 to 520,000, Henrico from 334,000 to 416,000, Richmond city from 227,000 to 276,000, and Hanover from 110,000 to 139,000. All four lines rise across the whole period.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **Chesterfield is projected to grow 43% by 2050, reaching about 520,000 residents — up from the 38% growth projected in the 2022 Framework.**
- Henrico (+25%, to 416,000), Hanover (+27%, to 139,000), and Richmond city (+22%, to 276,000) all continue growing, with no primary locality projected to plateau.

## Older adults becoming larger share of population


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Nearly one in three residents is now 55 or older](demand_files/figure-html/fig-age-1.png){#fig-age fig-align='left' fig-alt='Population pyramid of the four primary localities by age group and sex from the 2020-2024 ACS. The 25-34 age group is the largest. Residents 55 and older account for nearly a third of the population. Male and female bars are roughly symmetric, with women outnumbering men at ages 75 and over.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **Residents 55 and older make up 30% of the region's population, and residents 65 and older make up 17%.**
- The 25-34 age group is the region's single largest — prime household-formation years, which converts directly into near-term housing demand.
- Seniors 65+ living alone represent a meaningful share of all households in the four primary localities — a group with distinct needs for smaller, accessible, and lower-maintenance homes.
- Women outnumber men in the 75+ group, so older single-person households are disproportionately older women.

## Median household incomes continue to rise


::: {.cell layout-align="left"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![Households in every locality have seen incomes grow](demand_files/figure-html/fig-income-1.png){#fig-income fig-align='left' fig-alt='Dot plot of median household income for the four primary localities at three ACS vintages: 2014, 2019, and 2024. The 2014 point is muted grey; the 2019-to-2024 segment is highlighted. Richmond city is lowest in 2024 at about $65,000. All four localities show consistent income gains since both 2014 and 2019.' width=100%}
:::
:::


- **Every locality's median household income rose at least 23 percent since 2019.**
- Richmond city's median rose 37 percent since 2019 — from $47,250 to $64,587 — yet it remains the lowest among the four primary localities.
- The slowest income growth among the four primary localities since 2019 was in Chesterfield (+23%).
- Going back to 2014, every primary locality's median has risen at least 40% in nominal terms — a full decade of income growth that predates this recent acceleration.
- Each vintage is expressed in its own survey-year dollars, so these changes are nominal; part of the increase reflects inflation.

::: {.callout-note}
## Data caveats

- Population estimates for 2020-2025 are Census Bureau Vintage 2025 figures and will be revised in future vintages. Weldon Cooper projections are the 2025 release, benchmarked to the 2020 census.
- ACS income medians are 5-year averages in each vintage's own survey-year dollars. Comparisons across vintages are nominal, not inflation-adjusted.
- The 2022 Data Update baseline used 2016-2020 ACS and the prior Weldon Cooper release, so "Since 2022" comparisons reflect both real change and vintage revisions.
:::
